judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 3 (rank 3) Reading and Phonics Skills under the printed 'Group Guided Reading' sub-strand, so direction is set by Term within the grade. The second SFI sits in Term 3 ('Uses a range of self-correcting methods when reading: re-reading, reading on, pausing', identity scope term=term 3) and the first in Term 4 ('Monitors self when reading, both in the area of word recognition and comprehension', identity scope term=term 4), so only Term 3 -> Term 4 (second_to_first) is a valid developmental direction. The change is substantive rather than repeated wording: Term 3 names a concrete repertoire of fix-up actions applied while reading, while Term 4 requires the learner to self-monitor across two domains, word recognition and comprehension, i.e. to detect breakdowns independently and apply strategies in both decoding and meaning-making; the Term 4 row context also carries the self-correcting bullet alongside it, indicating the strategy repertoire is retained and extended. Fluent use of the Term 3 self-correcting methods plausibly supports success with the broader Term 4 self-monitoring demand. Both endpoints have truncated source evidence and upstream merge/audit context (Grade and Term banners are merged nodes), so this is an inference from the bounded excerpt rather than full-source confirmation.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 1 Reading and Phonics / Phonics skills (same Grade rank 1), but their identity scopes differ by Term: the second SFI is Grade 1 Term 1 oral phonemic awareness (blending sounds c-a-t into cat, segmenting words cat into c-a-t, consonant/vowel substitution word play), while the first SFI is Grade 1 Term 3 'Uses consonant blends to build up and break down words' (bl-ack, fl-op, sl-ip), set in a Term 3 context that revises single letters and introduces consonant blends and digraphs. Oral blending and segmenting proficiency directly supports success in blending and segmenting consonant-blend words, so the direction runs from the Term 1 statement to the Term 3 statement (second_to_first), which is a permitted earlier-Term-to-later-Term direction within Grade 1. Shared LC tags (segmenting, words, consonant) corroborate the phonological-manipulation coherence rather than being the sole basis.
